blurb: Medium British sighthound with explosive speed and a calm, gentle manner indoors
description: The Whippet is a medium-sized British sighthound between the Greyhound and Italian Greyhound in size, with a short smooth coat and a gentle, calm temperament.
answer: The Whippet is a British sighthound that sits between the Greyhound and the Italian Greyhound in size, once called the poor man's racehorse. It stands about 44–51 cm, has a short, smooth coat, and is described as gentle, affectionate and calm at home but fast and lively outdoors.

body: Greyhound-type dogs of several sizes are recorded in medieval hunting manuals, and the word whippet, from an old term meaning to move briskly, was first used for a dog in 1610. In Victorian England the breed, also called the snap-dog, was developed for catching rabbits, coursing, straight racing and showing.

Whippet racing was popular in northern England and Wales in the nineteenth century, often in rag races where dogs sprinted to owners waving towels. The AKC recognised the breed in 1888 and the Kennel Club in 1891, and Whippets have won Best in Show at Westminster and several times at Crufts.

The Whippet is sleek and aerodynamic, with a deep chest and long, slender legs. The ideal height is 44–47 cm for females and 47–51 cm for males, though North American standards allow larger dogs. Color is considered immaterial, so coats range from black to white, red, fawn, brindle, blue and cream. The coat is short, smooth and close, with no undercoat and little shedding.

Whippets are commonly described as gentle, quiet and affectionate; the AKC calls them quiet and dignified in the living room and excellent house dogs. They bond strongly with owners and may suffer separation anxiety. They are said to suit homes with children and pets, but a strong prey drive means they may chase cats, rabbits and squirrels.

The breed needs regular exercise, ideally chances for short, explosive sprints followed by long rests; it can reach about 56 km/h. Grooming needs are minimal, but low body fat and a thin coat make Whippets sensitive to cold, so a coat or sweater may be needed. Care is advised off-leash because of prey drive.

The Whippet is generally described as a healthy breed; a 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 13.4 years. Like other sighthounds it is intolerant of barbiturate anesthetics. Conditions reported include heart disease, notably mitral valve disease in older dogs, rare genetic eye defects, and a myostatin mutation that produces heavily muscled bully Whippets.

faq.a: Very little. Their short, smooth coat has no undercoat and is easy to care for.

faq.q: How fast can a Whippet run?
faq.a: Whippets can reach about 56 km/h and are considered the fastest dogs of their weight class.
